Agreed on next steps including sharing SOC2, enabling logs for 30 days, and scheduling a deep-dive.
topics: Redwood Dedicated vs Private network constraints
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-01-14
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Ava, Daniel, Maya (Redwood) / Rachel, Samir, Lori, Devon (Peregrine)
Links shared: [SOC2 attestation (placeholder link)], [pilot audit-log sample CSV], internal deck: https://redwood.example.com/pilot-security-deck (note: shared in meeting)

00:00 - Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We wanted to keep this tight — 45 minutes — go over the security blockers you flagged and make sure we have concrete next steps. Rachel, do you want to kick off with the high level?

00:18 - Rachel Ng: Yeah thanks Ava, um so overall pilot is going well from a functionality perspective, but for compliance we need to confirm SSO integration (Okta), audit logging retention, and get SOC2 evidence. We also have a few questions about KMS and whether Redwood Privet — sorry Redwood Private — can be air-gapped or needs a managed control plane.

00:39 - Daniel Cho: Totally. Quick correction: Redwood Private does provide a customer-controlled control plane option, but the default we ship uses a small control plane in our managed infra with VPC peering — you can opt for a private control plane for on-prem installs. We'll send the doc.

01:05 - Samir Patel: When you say control plane, are logs forwarded out of our VPC? We need assurance logs can be pushed to our SIEM; we can't have long-term copies stay with third parties beyond 30 days.

01:22 - Daniel Cho: Good question. For the hosted pilot we typically stream audit events to a customer-provided S3 or to our audit endpoint with retention configurable. For Dedicated and Private, you can route logs to your S3 or Splunk via an agent. The default retention on our console is 90 days, but for pilots we can enable a 30-day window and provide export.

01:45 - Lori Chen: That 90 days default — can we set it per-namespace? We have different data classification buckets.

02:02 - Ava Martinez: Yes, namespaces (or routes) can have per-retention policy, and we can scope log export by project. We'll share a sample retention policy.

02:20 - Devon Ortiz: Another infra constraint: does the KV cache ever get persisted outside memory? We worry about PII drifting into exported caches.

02:35 - Daniel Cho: KV cache is in-memory by default for low-latency inference; it isn't persisted to disk in our managed offering. If you enable certain persistence features for long-running sessions, those are optional and can be configured to encrypt at rest using your KMS. But standard pilot config keeps it ephemeral. Note: sometimes the transcript generator shows K V cache, uhm, but it's the in-memory KV cache.

03:01 - Samir Patel: Encryption at rest — we need to know if Redwood uses CMEK and whether we can supply keys via our AWS KMS / HSM.

03:15 - Maya Rivera: We support customer-managed keys in the Dedicated and Private tiers; for hosted we have envelope encryption and can integrate with AWS KMS via a customer-managed key for some customers under contract. We'll attach the KMS FAQ and a config snippet.

04:00 - Rachel Ng: Great. On SOC2, do you have the full Type II report? Our purchasing requires the report and a SOC2 attestation letter.

04:18 - Ava Martinez: Yes, we can share SOC2 Type II redacted report and the attestation letter. I'll drop them after the call. Also we have an encryption whitepaper that explains key lifecycle and HSM usage.

05:00 - Samir Patel: SSO: we're on Okta and we'd prefer SAML with signed assertions and SCIM for user provisioning. Are both supported?

05:18 - Daniel Cho: Yes, SAML SSO is supported; we also support OIDC. SCIM provisioning is supported in the console for Redwood Dedicated and Hosted accounts. For pilot, we can enable SCIM for automatic sync, but sometimes customers prefer to manual map groups at first.

05:40 - Devon Ortiz: What about session length and token revocation? We need short-lived tokens and the ability to force logout on a user.

06:00 - Daniel Cho: Session tokens are short-lived JWTs (default 1 hour) and we have immediate revocation hooks via the console. For additional constraints we can shorten TTLs and add token introspection calls to your IdP.

06:30 - Speaker 1: (inaudible)

07:00 - Rachel Ng: Ok, audit logs — what fields do you capture? We need user, action, resource, IP, request payload hashes, and response status.

07:25 - Daniel Cho: The audit record schema includes timestamp, user id, email, action type, resource id, route, request size, response status, and an event hash. We can also include correlation IDs and request headers per your compliance needs. We'll share the schema. Occasionally the auto-transcript writes 'event has' instead of 'event hash' — tiny glitch.

08:00 - Samir Patel: Are those logs structured JSON that we can ingest directly into Splunk?

08:10 - Daniel Cho: Yes JSON objects, newline-delimited, ready for Splunk, S3, or EventBridge. We can push to a pre-configured S3 bucket in your account; the pilot permission pattern is documented.

09:00 - Lori Chen: Regarding data residency, our EU customers need data to remain in eu-west-1. Does the pilot offer region pinning?

09:15 - Ava Martinez: We can route requests to eu-west-1 for your EU traffic; for pilot it's best-effort but for Dedicated/Private you can pin regions. We'll document how routing policies work and the fallback behavior if capacity isn't available.

10:00 - Rachel Ng: One compliance ask: do you provide immutable audit logs or append-only storage for tamper evidence?

10:20 - Daniel Cho: We support append-only S3 with Object Lock for immutability when configured to your bucket. Also we can generate signed audit digests for a given period to prove integrity.

11:00 - Samir Patel: If we set retention to 30 days and push to our S3 with Object Lock, do you still keep a copy? We need to know any retained backups or copies in Redwood's systems.

11:30 - Maya Rivera: For the pilot, we won't retain a second copy beyond what's configured — we'll route to your endpoint. For hosted product defaults there can be ephemeral copies for troubleshooting, but those are purged and encrypted; we'll provide the retention guarantees in the doc.

12:00 - Devon Ortiz: About network: we need to confirm whether traffic to the model endpoints touches public IPs or stays inside peered VPCs for Dedicated.

12:15 - Daniel Cho: For Dedicated, endpoints are inside your VPC; for Private we deploy in your network. For hosted, there are public endpoints but you can create private connectivity using a NAT or a shared VPC peering arrangement. We'll outline network topologies in the doc.

13:00 - Rachel Ng: A couple smaller asks — can we redact PII from logs before they hit storage? We want to ensure we don't persist sensitive user content.

13:20 - Daniel Cho: We have pre-log hooks that can scrub request payloads; you can register scrubbing rules or use regex filters. We also support on-the-fly masking and tokenization via a middleware layer. We'll put examples in the sample audit log export.

14:00 - Samir Patel: For the SOC2 evidence, we'll likely have an internal auditor ask about incident response timelines for model drift or data leaks. Can you share your incident response runbook?

14:20 - Ava Martinez: Yes, we have an IR runbook and incident SLA commitments for Dedicated customers. For hosted pilot we'll share the runbook and response RTOs/RPOs.

15:00 - Lori Chen: Anything about model outputs? We're doing embeddings and there's a concern about accidental storage of user-submitted PII in embeddings. Is there a deletion path?

15:20 - Daniel Cho: Embeddings are treated as user data. You can request deletion per dataset or per-namespace and we keep deletion logs. We also support hashed embeddings if you want a one-way transform.

16:00 - Rachel Ng: Good. On the SSO exchange, we need a metadata file from you for our Okta admin to import. Who's the best to provide that?

16:12 - Ava Martinez: I'll provide the SAML metadata, and Daniel will include example attribute mappings (email, groups). We should test assertions in your Okta sandbox.

16:45 - Samir Patel: SCIM — if we enable provisioning, do you enforce SCIM 2.0 spec and allow group syncs?

17:00 - Daniel Cho: Yes SCIM 2.0 with group-mapping is supported; we can also scope by group id so that only certain teams have access to pilot resources.

18:00 - Devon Ortiz: Can we get a short-lived credentials option for service-to-service calls instead of long-lived API keys?

18:20 - Daniel Cho: We have mTLS and short-lived token options; ephemeral credentials via AWS STS or similar can be wired up for Dedicated. For hosted we issue scoped API tokens with limited TTL and you can revoke them from the console.

19:00 - Speaker 2: (crosstalk)

20:00 - Ava Martinez: Ok, recap time. We've agreed to: 1) Ava to send SOC2 + encryption whitepaper; 2) Daniel to send audit-log schema + sample export and retention config; 3) enable a 30-day audit-log stream to Peregrine S3 for the pilot; 4) test Okta SAML metadata exchange and SCIM provisioning in your sandbox; 5) schedule the 60-min security deep-dive next week.

20:30 - Rachel Ng: That sounds good. Can we get the docs by EOD tomorrow? Our auditor wants to review initial artifacts quickly.

20:40 - Ava Martinez: Yes, I'll drop the SOC2 and whitepaper today, Daniel will have the audit sample tomorrow.

21:15 - Samir Patel: One last question — do you have any open pen-test results we can see?

21:28 - Maya Rivera: We have a penetration test report we can share redacted; it's part of the security pack. We'll include that and the vulnerability management cadence.

22:00 - Rachel Ng: Great. Next steps and owners please in the calendar invite. Thanks everyone.

22:20 - Ava Martinez: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts and calendar invite for the deep-dive.

End of meeting.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-attributions, slight background noise at minute ~19. Some product names transcribed as 'Redwood Privet' or 'K V cache'.
